title: AI makes measurement scalable while moving the bottleneck to construct definition and validation
source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35744, a methodological review of AI-generated variables and credible inference
geography: Economics research and AI-enabled measurement; general methodological evidence with implications for U.S. public, firm, and institutional measurement

denominator.unit: AI-generated measurement pipelines and validation settings; exact study count is not disclosed in the abstract

scalable_measurement.unit: feasibility of converting unstructured text and images into structured variables at low cost

measurement_bottleneck.unit: from finding any scalable measure toward choosing among plausible measures that can support different conclusions

pipeline_stages.unit: discovery, construct definition, and observation stages where AI enters measurement

institutional_boundary.value: measurement scale can increase while interpretive and legitimacy risk also increases

observations.method: Methodological review distinguishing discovery, construct definition, observation, validation samples, biased prediction, and settings without a random validation sample.
observations.uncertainty: This is a methodological review rather than a population estimate or causal evaluation of a specific AI system. The abstract does not disclose a systematic-review corpus count, and the framework does not by itself establish how a particular agency, firm, or public will implement validation.
observations.subgroup: Researchers, public agencies, firms, platforms, and communities whose classification, eligibility, risk, or performance may be represented through AI-generated variables; affected populations may experience consequences without seeing the construct or validation criteria.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower-cost measurement can improve visibility and enable measurement of previously inaccessible phenomena. Disagreement among plausible proxies may reflect legitimate multidimensionality rather than error, and explicit validation cannot eliminate all normative choices about what should be measured.

related_sources.claim: Official NBER DOI identifies the working paper.

boundary: This record establishes a methodological trend: AI can lower the cost of producing structured measures while increasing the importance of construct definition, validation, and interpretive governance. It does not establish accuracy, bias, discrimination, trust, policy effects, or outcomes for any particular U.S. population or institution.
